cohort: 86 pregnant women with Pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) and Deep venous thrombosis (DVT)
finding: The incidence of pulmonary thromboembolism and deep venous thrombosis was higher in the third trimester of pregnancy and postpartum, and vaginal delivery was associated with a lower risk of pulmonary thromboembolism than cesarean section.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery is safer than cesarean surgery with regards to pulmonary thromboembolism risk.
